title: English Language Centre Jobs in Ho Chi Minh City (2026)
description: How Saigon's English centres hire, schedule and pay in 2026: hourly rates from real job ads, the contract terms to check and the red flags before you sign.
h1: Working at an English language centre in Ho Chi Minh City: pay, hours and how to pick a good one
intro: Language centres are the most common job for foreign English teachers in Ho Chi Minh City: mostly children and teenagers, on weekday evenings and weekends, paid by the teaching hour, usually on 12-month contracts. Full-time typically means 20 to 25 teaching hours a week. Centres hire all year, and big chains such as VUS, ILA and Apollo recruit alongside many independent centres. Pick one by getting the hourly rate, guaranteed hours, pay date and your work permit in writing before your first class.
keyPoints: In July–October 2026 job ads, centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, with most new-teacher offers at {{vnd:430000-560000}}. 'Up to' figures are ceilings, not starting rates.
Apollo's full-time load in a 2024 listing, about 78–95 contact hours a month, works out at roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross a month at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour, before tax and insurance.
Expect weekday evenings and weekend days with children aged about 6–16. Hourly pay usually covers class time only, so ask about guaranteed hours, cancelled classes and the Tet closure.
Your work permit must be issued before your first paid class, probation included. Working without one costs {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and can lead to deportation (Decree 283/2026).
A centre may not take a deposit or keep your original passport or degree. Probation is at most 60 days at no less than 85% pay, and final pay is due within 14 working days.

sections.title: Who hires: the big chains and the independents

blocks.text: The market is large and moves fast. Ho Chi Minh City had 1,961 licensed foreign-language and IT centres in August 2025, 158 of them foreign-invested, according to the city's Department of Education and Training ([Tuoi Tre News](https://news.tuoitre.vn/ho-chi-minh-city-warns-language-centers-over-teacher-quality-especially-foreign-hires-103250925172100232.htm)). Churn is high: the city [dissolved or revoked 112 language and IT centres](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/ho-chi-minh-city-shuts-down-112-language-and-it-centers-2556885.html) during the 2025–26 school year while new ones opened.

Most foreign teachers work either for a **national chain** or for an independent centre with one or a handful of branches. Chains offer structure: a published hiring process, a few nights' accommodation on arrival (5 to 7 in VUS, ILA and Apollo ads), health insurance and work-permit sponsorship. Independents vary from excellent small schools to centres that pay late; you have to check each one yourself (see below).

Mostly young learners aged 3–17; teacher posts have asked for a degree plus CELTA, Trinity CertTESOL or equivalent; vacancies appear irregularly

blocks.text: Wall Street English also advertised part-time Ho Chi Minh City posts in May 2026 ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/ho-chi-minh-city-part-time-native-english-teachers-2)). Older guides still list employers that are gone: IDP's IELTS centre ACET [stopped operating in Vietnam on 31 December 2024](https://www.idp.com/vietnam/blog/official-acet-announcement/?lang=en), and the Apax Leaders children's chain collapsed owing wages ([VietnamFinance](https://vietnamfinance.vn/he-thong-te-liet-va-giai-the-apax-leaders-dang-no-ca-tram-ty-dong-d108066.html)).

eno.vn's [school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City's language centres among its employers, with their open jobs. Teachers who worked or interviewed at a centre can vote and write reviews, read by a moderator before they appear; most centres have few or no reviews yet, so treat it as a starting list and add what you know.

For current openings, eno.vn's [teaching jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) gathers centre postings from job boards and schools' own careers pages. A linked posting opens the original ad, where you apply, and expires within 14 days; eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them. Never pay to get a job.

One catch since 1 July 2025: Ho Chi Minh City absorbed Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau, so a job labelled 'HCMC' can be an hour or more from central Saigon. Job boards also tag some provincial campuses 'Hồ Chí Minh' ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh)). Ads still use old district names, but official addresses now use new ward names, so check the actual campus address before you compare offers.

Centre teaching follows the school day in reverse. VUS describes most classes as **weekday evenings and all day at weekends**, and defines full-time as 20–25 teaching hours a week and part-time as 12–18 ([VUS FAQ](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979)). An older Apollo ad for its Bien Hoa centre (about 2024) listed classes from 16:00 to 22:00 on weekdays and from 7:45 to 20:15 at weekends, so a weekend day can be long, with gaps between classes ([Apollo ad](https://teast.co/job/teaching-english-in-vietnam-bien-hoa-PYVxr1cMRTKp9amJSRu9)).

Hourly rates usually cover **contact time only**. Preparation, meetings, arriving early and travel between campuses are typically unpaid. Ask how many campuses you will rotate between; ILA's ad mentions rotation between locations.
Hourly, guaranteed or salaried

items: **Pure hourly**: you are paid for the hours you teach. Income falls when timetables shrink, over Tet and when classes are cancelled.

**Hourly with a guarantee**: some employers now advertise a 'guaranteed monthly salary' (Wall Street English) or a 'competitive guaranteed salary' (Apollo in Hanoi), but none publishes the amount. Get the guaranteed minimum hours or pay in writing.
**Monthly salary**: what bilingual schools and full-time kindergarten posts usually advertise; if a centre offers one, check how many teaching hours it covers.

blocks.text: The standard is a **12-month contract**, renewed yearly; VUS offers it after probation and once the work permit is issued. Whatever the paperwork is called, the [Labour Code](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html) treats an arrangement with paid work, a wage and the centre's supervision as a labour contract (Art. 13), and part-timers on labour contracts have the same rights as full-timers (Art. 32). A 'freelance' agreement with one centre that sets your timetable is still a labour contract in law, but it cannot support a work permit, which leaves you working without one.

Contracts of 12 months or more bring compulsory social insurance: you pay 9.5% (8% pension plus 1.5% health insurance) and the employer 20.5%, on salary capped at {{vnd:50600000}} a month from 1 July 2026 ([Vietnam Briefing](https://www.vietnam-briefing.com/doing-business-guide/vietnam/taxation-and-accounting/individual-income-tax)). To resign from a 12–36-month contract you give 30 days' notice; leaving without it costs half a month's salary plus pay for the missing notice days. Our guide to [teaching contracts](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam) goes through the clauses one by one.

Seasons matter too. Centres hire all year, busiest before and during the summer holiday (June–August) and slowest from mid-December until Tet, which falls on Saturday 6 February 2027 ([International TEFL Academy](https://www.internationalteflacademy.com/teach-english-in-vietnam)). See [finding a teaching job](/teach-in-vietnam/finding-a-teaching-job-in-vietnam) for timing your search.

As of October 2026, job ads put centre pay at {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, with most new-teacher offers between {{vnd:430000}} and {{vnd:560000}} ([Vietnam Teaching Jobs](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/city/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh)). Almost none of the ads say whether the rate is gross or net, and some quote US dollars, so ask which currency you will be paid in and at what exchange rate.

blocks.text: The tax figures come from PIT Law 109/2025/QH15: resident rates of 5/10/20/30/35% and a personal deduction of {{vnd:15500000}} a month ([KPMG](https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmg/vn/pdf/2026/01/new-pit-law-en.pdf)). Non-residents pay a flat 20%. Completion and KPI bonuses are usually lost if you leave early. For how centres compare with schools, kindergartens and agencies, see [English teacher salary in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam).

sections.title: Students, class sizes, teaching assistants and observations

blocks.text: Expect children and teenagers. VUS says most of its students are 6 to 16; the British Council teaches mostly 3- to 17-year-olds. Adult and exam classes tend to cluster in the evenings. IELTS is a big draw for teenagers, but a Ministry of Education draft published on 17 September 2026, still a draft in October 2026, would end university bonus points for IELTS from 2027, so do not build a career on it alone (see [teaching IELTS](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-ielts-in-vietnam)).

Classes are smaller than in public schools: teacher guides put private-centre classes at roughly 10–20 students, against 30–50 or more in public-school English ([Teast](https://teast.co/blog/public-vs-private-vietnam)). The centre rules in [Circular 21/2018](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-21-2018-tt-bgddt-quy-che-to-chuc-hoat-dong-cua-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-166595-d1.html) contain no class-size cap that we could find, so ask the maximum before you sign.

items: **Vietnamese teaching assistants**: young-learner classes commonly have one, and the British Council hires them for its city centres. Treat the TA as a co-teacher: brief them before class and agree when Vietnamese is acceptable. In some centres TAs also film children for parents.

**Observations**: VUS observes new teachers through their first month. Teachers commonly report scheduled and unannounced observations, and cameras in some classrooms that managers can watch. Ask for the observation rubric and any KPIs, such as re-enrolment or parent satisfaction.

**Parent feedback**: parents judge lessons by visible output such as worksheets, videos and short performances, and complaints usually reach you through the academic team. Communication runs largely on Zalo.

**Photos and videos**: since 1 January 2026, disclosing private information about a child needs a parent's consent, and from age 7 the child's own consent too ([Vietnam Lawyers' Journal](https://lsvn.vn/cong-bo-du-lieu-ca-nhan-cua-tre-tu-07-tuoi-phai-duoc-nguoi-dai-dien-dong-y-a167752.html)). Follow the centre's policy and never post students on your own accounts.

blocks.text: Quiet students are usually being respectful, not disengaged; our guide to [teaching young learners](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-young-learners-in-vietnam) covers classroom management for these ages.

sections.title: How centres hire, and when you can start teaching

blocks.text: Most centre interviews happen in person, but large chains interview overseas candidates by video: VUS uses an online form, then an HR video interview of about an hour. A demo lesson is common, sometimes taught to staff with no students present; ask beforehand who will watch, the learners' age and level, and how long it should run. The [CV and demo lesson guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-cv-and-demo-lesson-in-vietnam) has the details.

On paper, a centre teacher needs a college degree or higher plus a 'suitable' teaching certificate ([Circular 21/2018](https://luatvietnam.vn/giao-duc/thong-tu-21-2018-tt-bgddt-quy-che-to-chuc-hoat-dong-cua-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-166595-d1.html), Art. 18). The law sets no minimum course length; the [120-hour TEFL](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam) is an employer convention. Non-native speakers also need C1-level proof unless their degree is in the language or in language teaching. The work permit has its own test under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/decree-no-219-2025-nd-cp-dated-august-07-2025-of-the-government-on-foreign-workers-in-vietnam-407607-doc1.html), a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years' relevant experience. If you have less, ask the centre which proof it will file for you and get the answer in writing before you travel.

blocks.title: No paid class before the permit is issued
blocks.text: Probation and paid 'trial weeks' are not an exception. Under [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-283-2026-nd-cp-xu-phat-vi-pham-hanh-chinh-lao-dong-bao-hiem-xa-hoi-440485-d1.html), in force since 10 September 2026, a foreigner who works without a work permit is fined {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and can be deported. Ask to see your permit and check that the employer, job title and work location match what you will actually do. A second centre needs its own permit, even for weekend classes.

Probation is at most 60 days, at no less than 85% of the job's pay ([Labour Code](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html), Arts. 25–26). Your employer files the permit, and arranges the rest of your paperwork once it is issued; ask them exactly what they cover and what it costs, and whether any of it is clawed back if you leave early. The [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) covers the documents and timeline; your employer and the authority have the final word.

sections.title: How to check a centre before you sign

items.title: Pin down the legal entity
items.text: Ask for the company's full legal name and confirm the centre is licensed: the city's Department of Education and Training licenses centres ([SGGP](https://www.sggp.org.vn/tphcm-thanh-lap-7-so-moi-post782716.html)). The name on your contract should match the employer on your work permit. A licence is not proof of solvency: two licensed centres in Thu Duc shut suddenly in May 2025 after collecting tuition ([Tuoi Tre](https://tuoitre.vn/so-giao-duc-va-dao-tao-tp-hcm-bao-cao-vu-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-thu-hoc-phi-hang-ti-dong-roi-bien-mat-20250519213401173.htm)).

items.title: Check the recruiter is real
items.text: Match the email domain and website to the employer's own channels. VUS says genuine recruitment emails end in @vus-etsc.edu.vn and that any request for money or to download an app is a scam ([VUS warning](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/fake-job-warning)). More in [teaching job scams](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam).

items.title: Talk to teachers who work there now
items.text: Ask whether pay has been on time, how many hours they actually get and how cancellations are handled. In teacher forums, late pay is the problem most often reported at small schools. Look the centre up in the eno.vn [school directory](/schools), and leave a review afterwards.

items.title: Ask the money questions in writing
items.text: Use the list below and get the answers into the offer letter or contract, not a chat message.

items.title: Read the contract before you travel
items.text: Ask for a bilingual contract that states which language prevails, check the end date is no later than the permit's, and keep a signed copy.

items: Is the rate gross or net, per 60-minute hour or per shorter period, and paid in đồng or dollars?
What is the guaranteed minimum of hours or pay each month? Can I see the next four weeks' timetable?
Are preparation, meetings, training and observations paid?
What happens to my pay for cancelled classes, public holidays and the Tet closure?
On what date am I paid, and how? When is the first payday?
Which campuses will I teach at, and is travel between them paid?
Will I be enrolled in social and health insurance, and how is income tax calculated on my payslip?
What are the completion bonus conditions, and is it paid pro rata if the centre ends the contract early?

sections.title: Red flags at a language centre

blocks.caption: Warning signs and what the law says (Labour Code 2019, Decree 283/2026, city directives)
rows: Asks for a deposit or bond, or holds back your first month's pay as security

Banned by Labour Code Art. 17. Since 10 September 2026 the fine is {{vnd:20000000-25000000}}, doubled for a company, and the money must be returned ([VnExpress](https://vnexpress.net/phat-den-25-trieu-dong-voi-doanh-nghiep-giu-giay-to-cua-nguoi-lao-dong-5103298.html))
Wants to keep your original passport or degree
Also banned by Art. 17. Hand over certified copies; if the passport is needed briefly for filing, get a dated receipt
Wants you to start paid teaching before the permit is issued
You carry the {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} fine and the risk of deportation; the centre faces its own fines
Offers a 'freelance' or 'service' contract while setting your timetable
In law it is a labour contract (Art. 13), but it cannot support a work permit
Fines for lateness, or pay docked as discipline
Fines and wage cuts as discipline are prohibited (Art. 127). Full pay is due for classes cancelled through the centre's fault (Art. 99)
'Contract-breaking fees' on top of the Labour Code
The Code fixes what you owe for quitting unlawfully: half a month's salary plus the missing notice days, and training costs only under a written training contract (Arts. 40, 62)
Probation over 60 days or below 85% pay
Breaches Arts. 25–26
Pushes parents into long prepaid tuition packages

Apax collapsed owing parents tuition refunds ([VietnamFinance](https://vietnamfinance.vn/he-thong-te-liet-va-giai-the-apax-leaders-dang-no-ca-tram-ty-dong-d108066.html)) and two Úc Châu centres shut suddenly after collecting tuition ([Tuoi Tre](https://tuoitre.vn/so-giao-duc-va-dao-tao-tp-hcm-bao-cao-vu-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-thu-hoc-phi-hang-ti-dong-roi-bien-mat-20250519213401173.htm)); a city directive limits tuition to months actually studied ([VOH](https://voh.com.vn/giao-duc/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tai-tphcm-khong-duoc-thu-hoc-phi-dai-han-510985.html))
Current teachers report late pay
Pay that is 15 or more days late must carry interest (Art. 97), and you may resign without notice if you are not paid in full or on time, unless the delay is a force-majeure one of up to 30 days

blocks.text: If a centre does not pay, put your claim in writing and keep every payslip and transfer. After a contract ends the employer has 14 working days to settle everything (Art. 48). Wage complaints now go to the city's Department of Home Affairs, which took over labour matters in 2025 ([SGGP](https://www.sggp.org.vn/tphcm-thanh-lap-7-so-moi-post782716.html)); you have 6 months to ask for mediation and 1 year to go to court.

faqs.q: Which is better to work for: VUS, ILA, Apollo or the British Council?
faqs.a: No independent data ranks them. They differ in student ages, qualifications asked for and package details, and conditions vary by campus and manager. Compare written offers on guaranteed hours, rate, pay date and permit support, and ask current teachers at the campus you would join.

faqs.q: Can I teach at a second centre at weekends?
faqs.a: Not on your first employer's work permit. Under Decree 219/2025, working for another employer needs a new permit filed by that employer, even for the same job.

faqs.q: Do language centres hire non-native English speakers?
faqs.a: Yes, some do. VUS considers non-native speakers who send an intro video. By law a non-native teacher at a centre needs a degree in language teaching, a degree in English plus a teaching certificate, or any degree plus C1-level proof and a teaching certificate (Circular 21/2018, Art. 18).

faqs.q: Do centres pay hourly teachers over Tet?
faqs.a: Often not: many hourly arrangements pay only for hours taught, and teaching guides say centres usually close for about 7 to 10 days. Employees on labour contracts are entitled to paid public holidays, but how that works for hourly staff is not settled, so get the centre's answer in writing.

faqs.q: How soon after starting do I get paid?
faqs.a: Teachers report being paid monthly in arrears, so the first payday can be about a month after your first class. Bring enough money to cover two to three months while your hours build up.
